title: The one incarnate Word suffers in flesh and works miracles in divinity, inseparably woven
english: This man despoiled death as God. Again the soldiers guarded him as a dead man, and the gatekeepers of Hades, seeing him as God, cowered in fear. You will say that he is the same one in both: the one who suffers and the one who works wonders. He is not one and another, not one person inside another, not one acting through another. For the incarnate Word, being one, gathered these things and those into one by an ineffable word, as he willed. He gave the flesh to serve the sufferings, and he employed his divinity for the signs and the miracles. But just as it is not right for the Word to be separated from the flesh, so the sufferings must be interwoven with the miracles.
translator_notes: The section opens in mid-sentence; its first word, ἄνθρωπος, is rendered at the end of the previous section ('as a man…').
πυλωροὶ τοῦ ᾅδου ... ἔπτηξαν echoes Job 38:17 LXX (πυλωροὶ δὲ ᾅδου ἰδόντες σε ἔπτηξαν).
ἀρρήτῳ λόγῳ: 'in a manner beyond telling'; Hesychius plays on Λόγος, the Word, and λόγῳ, 'telling'.
ἐπεί πως ... πὼς δὲ ... πὼς δὲ: read as ἐπεὶ πῶς, 'otherwise, how...?', the argument that only God's presence explains the angels at the tomb.
The angels' words run on into the next section; the quotation is split there with an ellipsis.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia ii in sanctum pascha (Khazarzar) u01 rem early
orientation: Hesychius continues showing how Jesus was treated as dead by human actors but revealed as God by divine power, insisting these are not two persons but the single incarnate Word whose sufferings and miracles are inextricably interwoven.

title: Angels announce the empty tomb
english: For the one who went down into Hades as one dead freed the dead as God. See how angels minister at the tomb, how they appear to the women wearing white garments as for a bridegroom, and how they spoke to them: "You seek Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He is not here, for he has risen, as he said (cf. Mark 16:6; Matthew 28:6). This means heaven is his place, so send the ointments there. He has risen; we did not raise him. We rolled the stone away for your sake, for the tomb already stood empty before we came down. He has risen, as he himself said."

What the angel said, not even a prophet can fully interpret. Hosea tells the time of the Resurrection, and Isaiah knows it, but he does not know how it happens. For these are Hosea's words of prophecy: "Let us go and return to the Lord our God, for he has struck us and he will heal us. He will strike us and bind us up after two days; on the third day we shall rise and live before him (Hosea 6:1-2)."
Listen again to what Isaiah trumpeted: "Lebanon is ashamed, Sharon has become a marsh (Isaiah 33:9)."
translator_notes: The section opens inside the angels' words begun in the previous section ('You are looking for Jesus…'). The first sentence blends Mark 16:6 (Ἰησοῦν ζητεῖτε τὸν Ναζαρηνὸν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον) and Matthew 28:6 (οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν); the rest of the speech is Hesychius' own expansion and is not cited.
Hosea 6:1–2: Hesychius reads πέπαικεν ('has struck') for the Septuagint's ἥρπακεν (the edition sets the word outside the quotation marks) and leaves out ὑγιάσει; the English follows his wording.
Isaiah 33:9a follows the Septuagint (ᾐσχύνθη 'put to shame', ἕλη 'marshes'), not the Hebrew 'withers ... like a desert'. The quotation continues in the next section.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia ii in sanctum pascha (Khazarzar) u01 rem mid
orientation: Hesychius the homilist continues his proof that the one incarnate Word both died and as God freed the dead, now giving what the angels said to the women.

title: What each now means
english: "Galilee shall be seen, and Carmel shall be revealed. Now I will rise, says the Lord; now I will be glorified; now I will be exalted. Now you shall see; now you shall be put to shame (Isaiah 33:9-11)."

For Isaiah directed this word to the Jews. "Now I will rise" means, when I raise Adam, whom transgression cast down. "Now I will be glorified" means, when I establish for the nations impassibility from sufferings. "Now I will be exalted" means, as I lift your firstfruits to heaven and raise to the seat of the cherubim the form of a servant which I have taken from you.

"Now you shall see" means, as you watch the types come to an end and the truth bloom. "Now you shall be put to shame" means, as you slander with words and are defeated by deeds. To God be the glory, to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
translator_notes: The section opens in the middle of the quotation of Isaiah 33:9–11, which begins at the end of the previous section ('Lebanon has been put to shame; Sharon has become marshland'); the citation stands at the close of the quoted verses.
φανερὰ ἔσται: Septuagint 'will be manifest, exposed'; rendered 'will be laid bare'.

Πρὸς … τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τὸν λόγον ἀπετείνετο: 'he was directing these words at the Jews'. The following clauses are the Lord's own first-person voice, expounding each 'now' of the verse, so they are set in double quotation marks; the doxology after ὅτι is the preacher's close and stands outside them.

τοῖς ἔθνεσιν τῶν παθῶν συστήσω τὴν ἀπάθειαν: ἀπάθεια with a genitive of what one is free from, 'freedom from the passions'. Hesychius plays on παθῶν / ἀπάθειαν; τῶν παθῶν could also be read as 'through (my) sufferings', giving 'when through my sufferings I establish freedom from suffering for the nations'. The plainer construction is kept and the alternative noted here.

τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀπαρχήν: 'your firstfruits', the human nature Christ took 'from you' (ἐξ ὑμῶν), that is, from Israel; it is the same as 'the form of the servant' in the next phrase. A link with 1 Corinthians 15:20 (ἀπαρχή) is possible but the wording is not close enough to cite inline.

εἰς τὴν καθέδραν τῶν χερουβίν: 'to the throne of the cherubim', the seat of God above the cherubim. It may recall Psalm 79:2 LXX (Psalm 80:1, ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῶν χερουβίν), but the wording differs, so it is not cited inline.
παυομένους τοὺς τύπους, ἀνθοῦσαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν: the Old Testament types ceasing and the truth they foreshadowed 'in flower'.
συκοφαντοῦντες ῥήμασιν καὶ ἡττώμενοι πράγμασιν: the contrast is words against deeds; πράγμασιν rendered 'the facts', the events of the Resurrection that refute the slander.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia ii in sanctum pascha (Khazarzar) u01 rem close
orientation: Hesychius completes the Isaiah quotation and then expounds each now clause as the Lord speaking about raising Adam and exalting humanity.
